reason: The frozen deposit's own byline states 'DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21632723' on a file whose version line says 1.3. Live Zenodo says otherwise, and the deposit is wrong. It is NOT corrected: the deposited artifact is the historical record of what was published, defects included, and a deposit is fixed at the deposit or not at all. THE INFERENCE THIS ITEM EXISTS TO BLOCK: a checker that sees this token tolerated in a v1.3 file must not conclude that 21632723 IS the v1.3 record. Historical-artifact truth and current bibliographic truth are different registers, and the exception is granted to the FILE, never to the CLAIM. specs/open_planner/README.md is not the deposit — it is a current document making a current claim — and was corrected to 21695710 on 2026-08-21; it still names 21632723 correctly, as v1.0.

reason: The defect is in EXTERNAL metadata and can only be fixed by editing the Zenodo deposit; nothing in this repo can repair it. truth: 22018549 = A Primer on the Theory of Data v2.2 (concept 21842993). 22018598 = The Theory of Data: An Introduction v2.2 (concept 21763394). 21960380 = A Primer on the Theory of Data Applied v1.0 (concept 21960379). 21959941 = The Theory of Data Applied v1.0 (concept 21959940). Four DISTINCT works.
reason: No defect — a standing hazard, recorded so it is not rediscovered by accident. 22018549 and 22018598 are 49 apart, were deposited on the same day, and carry the SAME version string (2.2) on DIFFERENT works. A reader reconciling by title-prefix or by eye will fuse them. Separately, the three 'Primer / Applied' titles are three separate works with three separate concept records and NO supersession edge between them: their cross-references are relationships, not version identity. That ruling is encoded in works.json — each has its own workId and its own conceptRecid — and this row is the human-readable warning beside it.

Three things follow and all three are done: it stops being treated as publication authority (its class here is frozen-corpus, and no derived surface reads it); it is recorded as a remaining manual/frozen consumer (consumers.json); and the registry knows the current truth independently of it. claim: 10.5281/zenodo.21959749 is the current record of Analytical Governance
truth: 21959749 is v1.0 (2026-08-15), superseded 2026-08-21 by v1.1 (10.5281/zenodo.22046037). Both remain historically addressable; Zenodo's own metadata on v1.1 carries isNewVersionOf 10.5281/zenodo.21959749.
reason: RETIRED AS CURRENT AUTHORITY, NOT RETIRED. v1.0 is a first-class historical record and this item does not forbid its DOI — it forbids the CLAIM that it is current. Version history, supersession relationships, dated reconciliation checkpoints and frozen v1.0 material may all name it, and three tracked documents legitimately do. What may not name it is a current publication view: /about, the llms publication inventory, and the /analytical-governance citation. Those three are class `derived` and carry no literal DOI at all, so the prohibition is structural rather than advisory — they re-derived to v1.1 the moment the record landed, with no edit to any page.

claim: The registry models The Silent Failure Atlas as exactly the deposits of Zenodo concept 20762838
truth: Concept 20710592 holds 10.5281/zenodo.20710593 — Atlas v1.2, 2026-06-16 — and concept 20762838 holds 10.5281/zenodo.20762839, v1.3, 2026-06-19. v1.3's own Zenodo description reads 'New addition of MIN/MAX pattern, updated from v1.2'. One intellectual work, deposited twice under two separate concept records; the registry models the second only.
reason: NOT A DATA GAP — A MODEL GAP, and therefore not closed inside the unit that found it. Work.conceptRecid is single-valued and G4 fails any record whose snapshot concept differs from its work's declared concept, so v1.2 can be filed under w-silent-failure-atlas only by breaking G4, or as its own work only by asserting there are two Atlases. Leaving it out is the least false of the three and is what the registry does; this row is the record that it is a choice, not an oversight. The ruling required is whether a Work may ATTACH MORE THAN ONE concept identity — which the existing doctrine ('a later deposit attaches an external concept identity to an existing datumwise work') already leans toward. That is a schema change to works.json, G1 and G4, and belongs to its own unit. Meanwhile the current record of the Atlas is v1.3 and nothing on the property is wrong. See specs/publication_corpus_coverage_v0_1.md §4.1.
provenance: Phase 3B creator sweep, 2026-08-21: q=metadata.creators.person_or_org.name:"Wang, Huayin" returned 34 latest-version records, of which concept 20710592 is one the registry does not claim. Live Zenodo verified the same day.

claim: 10.5281/zenodo.21893929 ('Three Structural Sources of Silent Analytical Failure', v2.0, 2026-08-11) declares isNewVersionOf 10.5281/zenodo.21553379 ('The Two Great Sources of Silent Analytical Failure', unversioned, 2026-07-25)
truth: The claim is Zenodo's, made in 21893929's own metadata, and it crosses a concept boundary: 21553379 is concept 21553378 and 21893929 is concept 21893928. The registry models w-two-great-sources as concept 21553378 alone, so 21553379 remains its current record and is rendered as such by /about and the llms.txt inventory.
reason: OPEN, AND STATED AS OPEN. If the successor claim is ratified, /about and llms.txt are today rendering stale current authority — the exact defect this registry exists to end — and the registry CANNOT EXPRESS THE REPAIR: G3 requires supersession edges to stay inside one work, and a work may hold one concept. Three readings, none of them a checker's to pick: (1) one work, two concepts, one chain — needs rc-atlas-two-concepts' multi-concept attachment and then falls out for free; (2) two works, related — needs a relationship edge between works, which the model deliberately does not have; (3) a deposit defect, isNewVersionOf asserted where a reference was meant, in which case nothing changes and this row retires. NOTHING IS CURRENTIZED ON A GUESS: the token is permitted only in the coverage ledger that reports it, and is forbidden on every derived surface, so the open question cannot leak onto a page while it is open. See specs/publication_corpus_coverage_v0_1.md §4.2.
provenance: Phase 3B creator sweep, 2026-08-21. Live Zenodo: 21893929 related_identifiers = [{isNewVersionOf, 10.5281/zenodo.21553379}].

reason: NO DEFECT — A DECLARED BOUNDARY. The registry has never modeled the whole deposited corpus; it models what the property cites plus what has been ruled in, and Phase 3B was scoped to the Evidence pillar. Neither of these is an Evidence work. They are recorded rather than quietly onboarded because minting a work means NAMING it, which is the one genuinely editorial act in this system and does not get done as a side effect of a unit about something else. Each is one line of works.json plus one seed whenever it is wanted. Until then this row is what stops the gap from being rediscovered as a surprise. The forbiddenContexts entry is the operative half: an unmodeled work may be NAMED in the coverage ledger and may not be CITED on a derived surface, because a derived surface cites the registry and the registry does not know these.
